A former First Mayor of Hamburg and finance minister, this Social Democrat succeeded Angela Merkel as Germany's leader, serving as chancellor from 2021 to 2025 — who is he?
Olaf Scholz: Chancellor of Germany from 2021 to 2025. Olaf Scholz (born 14 June 1958) is a German politician who served as the chancellor of Germany from 2021 to 2025.

This 19th-century South American conflict was the deadliest interstate struggle in Latin American history, pitting one nation against an allied trio of neighboring countries from 1864 to 1870 — which conflict?
Paraguayan War: Major international war in South America (1864–1870)
A close ally of Robespierre, this French revolutionary chose suicide over arrest when authorities stormed the Hôtel de Ville during the coup of 9–10 Thermidor — who was he?
Born in London to a Ugandan-Indian family, this Conservative MP for Witham served as Home Secretary from 2019 to 2022 before becoming Shadow Foreign Secretary — who is she?

As Sweden's special envoy in Budapest in 1944 he saved thousands of Jews with protective passports and "Swedish territory" safe houses, then vanished in 1945 after Soviet SMERSH agents detained him — who was this humanitarian diplomat?
Raoul Wallenberg: Swedish diplomat and humanitarian (1912–1945). Raoul Wallenberg (4 August 1912 – disappeared 17 January 1945) was a Swedish architect, businessman, diplomat, and humanitarian.
The longest-serving prime minister in Slovak history, he has led the country across four separate terms since founding his left-wing party in 1999 — who is he?
Prince Albert Victor, Duke of Clarence and Avondale
Robert Fico: Prime Minister of Slovakia (2006–2010, 2012–2018, 2023–present)
After serving as Prime Minister of Kuwait from 1978 to 2006, this royal briefly became Emir for just nine days before abdicating — who is he?
Saad Al-Salim Al-Sabah: Emir of Kuwait in 2006.
Anointed by the prophet Samuel as the first king of a newly unified Israelite kingdom, he died falling on his own sword after defeat by the Philistines at Mount Gilboa — who was he?
Saul: Biblical figure and Israelite monarch.
This Indian politician served four terms as Chief Minister of Maharashtra and founded a new party in 1999 after splitting from the Indian National Congress — who is he?
Sharad Pawar: Indian politician. Sharadchandra Govindrao Pawar (born 12 December 1940) is an Indian politician who has served as a Member of Parliament, Rajya Sabha since 2014.

In just 96 hours of 1967, Israel captured the West Bank, Gaza, the Sinai Peninsula, and the Golan Heights from three Arab nations—a lightning campaign that reshaped the Middle East. What is this brief but transformative war called?
Six-Day War: 1967 war between Israel and Arab states.
This retired US Airways pilot safely ditched his disabled airliner on the Hudson River in January 2009 after a bird strike knocked out both engines, saving all 155 aboard — who is he?
Sully Sullenberger: American pilot and diplomat (born 1951)
Born Namgyal Wangdi, this Sherpa mountaineer stood atop Mount Everest alongside Edmund Hillary in 1953, becoming one of the first two confirmed to reach the summit — who is he?

The third son of Japan's founding Edo-period shōgun, this samurai ruled as the second shōgun of that dynasty from 1605 until his 1623 abdication, and became grandfather to Empress Meishō — who was he?
Tokugawa Hidetada: Japanese Samurai, Daimyo and Military ruler of Japan from 1605 to 1623.
With Merlin's magic making him look like his rival Gorlois, this legendary British king slept with Lady Igraine and fathered a certain 'once and future king' — who was he?
Uther Pendragon: Father of King Arthur in Arthurian legend.
Credited with coining the phrase 'sovereign democracy' while shaping Kremlin strategy for over a decade, this close Putin aide earned the nickname 'grey cardinal' — who is he?
As chief of the OKW, this German field marshal signed the criminal orders that fed countless war crimes — and was so deferential to Hitler that colleagues reviled him. Who was he?
Founded in London in 1844 by George Williams to promote 'muscular Christianity,' this youth organization now serves over 64 million people worldwide?
YMCA: Worldwide youth organization. YMCA is a worldwide youth organization based in Vernier, Canton of Geneva, Switzerland, with more than 64 million beneficiaries in 120 countries.
Emerging in late-19th-century Europe in reaction to antisemitism and led by Theodor Herzl, this nationalist movement sought a Jewish homeland in Palestine — what is it?
Zionism: Jewish nationalist movement. The arrival of Zionist settlers in Palestine during this period is widely seen as marking the start of the Israeli–Palestinian conflict.
Which of these four is the eldest?
Levi Strauss (born 1829) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four is the eldest?
Benjamin Banneker (born 1731) is the earliest of the four. Benjamin Banneker (November 9, 1731 – October 19, 1806) was an American naturalist, mathematician, astronomer and almanac author.
Which of these four was founded earliest?
C (programming language) (founded 1972) is the earliest of the four. C is a general-purpose programming language created in the 1970s by Dennis Ritchie.
Which of these four was founded earliest?

Lisp (programming language) (founded 1958) is the earliest of the four. Originally specified in the late 1950s, it is the second-oldest high-level programming language still in common use, after Fortran.
Which of these four is a physicist?
Roger Joseph Boscovich is a physicist.
Which of these four is a chemist?
Percy Lavon Julian is a chemist. Percy Lavon Julian (April 11, 1899 – April 19, 1975) was an American research chemist and a pioneer in the chemical synthesis of medicinal drugs from plants.
What is the atomic number of Mendelevium?
Mendelevium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Md (formerly Mv) and atomic number 101.
In what year was Grigori Perelman born?
Grigori Perelman: The full details of Perelman's work were filled in and explained by various authors over the following several years.
In what year was Sean Parker born?
Sean Parker: According to Forbes, as of May 2025, Parker's estimated net worth stood at US$3.0 billion, placing him in the top 1,250 richest individuals in the world.
In what year was C. V. Raman born?
C. V. Raman: This phenomenon, a hitherto unknown type of scattering of light they called modified scattering, was subsequently termed the Raman effect or Raman scattering.
In what year did Hypatia die?
Hypatia: Not the only fourth century Alexandrian female mathematician, Hypatia was preceded by Pandrosion.
In what year did Jan Hus die?
Jan Hus: Hus is considered to be the first Church reformer, even though some designate the theorist John Wycliffe.
In what year was Radium discovered?
Radium is a chemical element; it has symbol Ra and atomic number 88.
In what year was Copper discovered?
Copper is a chemical element; it has symbol Cu (from Latin cuprum) and atomic number 29.
Mil Mi-17: Kazan Helicopters. It is known as the Mi-8M series in Russian service.
Which country is Curtiss P-40 Warhawk from?
Curtiss P-40 Warhawk: United States. The Curtiss P-40 Warhawk is an American single-engined, single-seat, all-metal fighter-bomber that first flew in 1938.
Who is credited with discovering Ruthenium?
Ruthenium: Karl Ernst Claus. Ruthenium is a chemical element; it has symbol Ru and atomic number 44.
Who is credited with discovering Aniline?
Aniline: Otto Unverdorben. Aniline (From Portuguese: anil, meaning 'indigo shrub', and -ine indicating a derived substance) is an organic compound with the formula C6H5NH2.
Who is credited with discovering Lie group?
Lie group: Sophus Lie. Combining these two ideas, one obtains a continuous group where multiplying points and their inverses is continuous.
With the formula (CH3)2CO, this volatile solvent is produced by the millions of tonnes yearly, much of it to make precursors for plastics like bisphenol A — what is it?
Acetone (2-propanone or dimethyl ketone) is an organic compound with the formula (CH3)2CO.
A close relative of the peach in the genus Prunus, this drupe's seed isn't a true nut and can be "blanched" by softening its skin in hot water before peeling — what is it?
Nicknamed 'the heart of the scorpion,' this distinctly reddish variable star is the brightest in the constellation Scorpius — what is it?
Antares is the brightest star in the constellation of Scorpius. It has the Bayer designation α Scorpii, which is Latinised to Alpha Scorpii.
A methyl ester built from aspartic acid and phenylalanine, this non-saccharide sweetener is among the most-studied food additives ever, judged safe by over 100 regulatory bodies — what is it?
Aspartame is an artificial, non-saccharide sweetener commonly used as a sugar substitute in foods and beverages.
Their foliage is almost indistinguishable from a cycad's, but flower-like reproductive organs — some likely insect-pollinated — set these common Mesozoic seed plants apart. Which extinct order?
Bennettitales (also known as cycadeoids) is an extinct order of seed plants that first appeared in the Permian period and became extinct in most areas toward the end of the Cretaceous.
What hydrated mineral salt of sodium, mined economically in only a few places worldwide, forms a white crystalline solid that can be dehydrated by heating?
Borax (also referred to as sodium borate, tincal and tincar) is a salt (ionic compound) normally encountered as a hydrated borate of sodium, with the chemical formula Na2H20B4O17.

Native to tropical Africa, this vine's fruit can be eaten young as a vegetable, or left to mature, dry out, and be hollowed into a ladle, bowl, drinking vessel, or musical instrument — name this plant?

Calabash (Lagenaria siceraria), also known as bottle gourd, white-flowered gourd, long melon, birdhouse gourd, New Guinea bean, New Guinea butter bean, Tasmania bean, zucca melon and opo squash, is a vine which is grown for its fruit.

A cultivated variety of the same species as cabbage and broccoli, this vegetable's edible part is a dense head of undeveloped flower buds called the curd — one variety, Romanesco, grows its curds in stunning fractal spirals. Name this vegetable?
A notorious household nuisance pest that feeds on sleeping humans, this insect has never been shown to actually transmit disease to people — what is it?
Cimex lectularius is a species of Cimicidae.
This common bowel condition causes hard, dry stools passed fewer than three times a week, sometimes leading to hemorrhoids or fissures — what is it?
Constipation is a bowel dysfunction that makes bowel movements infrequent or hard to pass.
First created in 1994 and named for the German city where it was made, this synthetic element with atomic number 110 sits below platinum on the periodic table — what's it called?
Darmstadtium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Ds and atomic number 110.
Native to western North America, this towering conifer is also nicknamed Oregon pine or Columbian pine, though it isn't truly a pine at all — which tree?
Douglas fir (Pseudotsuga menziesii) is an evergreen conifer species in the pine family, Pinaceae.
Not a single disease but a syndrome of overall brain dysfunction with many possible causes, this term's Greek roots literally mean 'brain suffering' — what is it called?
Encephalopathy (from Ancient Greek (enkphalos) 'brain' and (pthos) 'suffering') is any disorder or disease of the brain, especially chronic degenerative conditions.
Known for filling pillows and blankets as well as lining the wings of birds, what are these soft, complex integumentary structures called?
Feather are epidermal growths that form a distinctive outer covering, or plumage, on both avian (bird) and some non-avian dinosaurs and other archosaurs.

This American mechanical engineer and pioneering management consultant wrote a 1909 book that Academy of Management fellows later voted the most influential management book of the entire 20th century — who was he?
Frederick Winslow Taylor (March 20, 1856 - March 21, 1915) was an American mechanical engineer.

Encoded by the codons CAA and CAG and structurally related to glutamic acid but with an amide in place of a carboxylic acid group, this charge-neutral amino acid becomes essential under bodily stress — which amino acid?
Glutamine (symbol Gln or Q) is an -amino acid that is used in the biosynthesis of proteins.
Newborns with this severe genetic skin disorder are born encased in thick, diamond-shaped plates separated by deep cracks that restrict movement and breathing — what is it?
Harlequin-type ichthyosis is a genetic disorder that results in thickened skin over nearly the entire body at birth.

Which field of study leans on anthropology, paleontology, and genetics to trace how our ancestors gradually picked up bipedalism, dexterity, and complex language — a story that turned out to be weblike rather than a tidy straight line?
Human evolution is a distinct species of the hominid family of primates, which includes all the great apes.
Usually caused by the Epstein–Barr virus and nicknamed 'glandular fever,' which illness brings fever, sore throat, swollen neck nodes, and a fatigue that can linger for months?
Infectious mononucleosis (IM, mono), also known as glandular fever, is an infection usually caused by the Epstein-Barr virus (EBV).
This self-described 'constitutional law attorney' joined Trump's inner circle in November 2019, though reporters found she'd never argued a federal case — who is she?
Jenna Ellis (born November 1, 1984) is an American conservative suspended lawyer who was a member of Donald Trump's 2020 re-election campaign's legal team.
The world's longest venomous snake with an average length of 3.18 to 4 meters, endemic to Asia and widely distributed though not commonly encountered. What is it?
King cobra (Ophiophagus hannah) is a species complex of snakes endemic to Asia.
This Soviet theoretical physicist laid the foundations of twentieth-century condensed matter physics and explained the theory behind superfluid helium — who is he?
Lev Landau (22 January 1908 - 1 April 1968) was a Soviet physicist who made fundamental contributions to many areas of theoretical physics.
Its name is Latin for 'wolf,' and this autoimmune disease cycles between flares and remission, often announcing itself with a red rash across the face — what is it?
Lupus (SLE), is an autoimmune disease in which the body's immune system mistakenly attacks healthy tissue in many parts of the body.

Encompassing complex, functional, and measure theory as major subfields, this branch of mathematics studies real numbers, sequences, series, and limits with rigor formalized in the 19th century — which field?
Mathematical analysis is the branch of mathematics that studies functions, spaces, and operators through quantitative methods of approximation and convergence.
Carrying the NATO reporting name 'Halo,' this Soviet/Russian heavy transport helicopter is the largest of its kind ever to enter serial production — name the aircraft?
Mil Mi-26 is a Soviet/Russian heavy transport helicopter.
Likened to insulation on an electrical wire, this fatty material sheaths axon segments to speed up the transmission of nerve impulses — what is it called?

Myelin is a lipid-rich material that in most vertebrates surrounds the axons of neurons to insulate them and increase the rate at which electrical impulses (called action potentials) pass along the axon.
Nicknamed the 'winter vomiting disease' and the most common cause of gastroenteritis, this fecal–orally spread bug usually strikes about 24 hours after exposure. What is it?
Norovirus is the most common cause of gastroenteritis. Norovirus, also known as Norwalk virus, is the most common cause of gastroenteritis.
Part of the Bovidae family, this genus of seven social species is better known simply as sheep, all thought to trace back to the wild mouflon — which genus?
Ovis is a genus of mammals, part of the Caprinae subfamily of the ruminant family Bovidae.
This flowering plant is the sole genus in its own botanical family and ranges from knee-high herbaceous perennials to woody shrubs over ten feet tall — what plant is it?
Peony is any flowering plant in the genus Paeonia, the only genus in the family Paeoniaceae.
Native to Eurasia and identifiable by short, blue-green needles, this member of the pine family goes by several regional common names — name the species (Latin binomial)?
Pinus sylvestris is a species of tree in the pine family Pinaceae that is native to Eurasia.

This oral glucocorticoid medication suppresses the immune system and reduces inflammation in conditions like asthma and COPD, though long-term use risks side effects such as cataracts and bone loss — what's the drug called?
Prednisone is a glucocorticoid medication mostly used to suppress the immune system and decrease inflammation in conditions such as asthma, COPD, and rheumatologic diseases.
This root vegetable in the mustard family, whose entire plant (leaves included) is edible, was domesticated in Asia and is now grown worldwide — what vegetable is it?
Radish (Raphanus sativus or Raphanus raphanistrum subsp.
This British economist won the 1991 Nobel Memorial Prize and warned that the field was "suicidal" to become a hard science of choice while ignoring society, history, and culture — who was he?
Ronald Coase (29 December 1910 - 2 September 2013) was a British economist and author.
Caused by a lack of vitamin C, this deficiency disease shows up after about a month of poor diet with weakness, sore limbs, gum disease, and bleeding from the skin — what is it?
Scurvy is a deficiency disease (state of malnutrition) resulting from a lack of vitamin C (ascorbic acid).
Famous for their slowness, these tree-dwelling Neotropical mammals are closest relatives of anteaters and come in just seven living species across two genera — what are they?
Sloth are a Neotropical group of xenarthran mammals constituting the suborder Folivora, including the extant arboreal tree sloths and extinct terrestrial ground sloths.
Director of research at Cambridge's Centre for Theoretical Cosmology, he was the Lucasian Professor of Mathematics from 1979 to 2009. Who?

Stephen Hawking (8 January 1942 - 14 March 2018) was an English theoretical astrophysicist, cosmologist, and author who was director of research at the Centre for Theoretical Cosmology at the University of Cambridge.
Found naturally in grapes and other fruits, this crystalline compound's potassium salt is better known as cream of tartar, a key ingredient in homemade baking powder — which compound?
Tartaric acid is a white, crystalline organic acid that occurs naturally in many fruits, most notably in grapes but also in tamarinds, bananas, avocados, and citrus.
This family of large, long-legged flies can be identified by a maxillary-palp segment longer than the other three combined, and typically has thirteen segments in each antenna. Name the family?
Tipulidae is a family of large crane flies in the order Diptera.
This medical specialty, whose name derives from the Greek word for urine, covers surgical and medical treatment of the urinary tract and the male reproductive organs — name this field?

Urology (from Greek ouron "urine" and - -logia "study of"), also known as genitourinary surgery, is the branch of medicine that focuses on surgical and medical diseases of the urinary system and the male reproductive organs.
Packing a mass comparable to the Sun into a volume the size of Earth, this dense stellar remnant radiates residual heat rather than nuclear fusion — what is it?
White dwarf is a very dense type of star: in an Earth-sized volume, it packs a mass that is comparable to the Sun.
This Danish physicist shared the 1975 Nobel for work on the structure of the atomic nucleus — making him and his famous father one of the rare parent-child pairs to each win the prize. Who was he?
Native to the arid Americas, most rosettes of this succulent genus flower gloriously just once before dying, earning one species the nickname 'century plant' — what genus is it?
Meaning 'different lizard' and first described in 1877 by Othniel Marsh, most fossils of this Late Jurassic predator come from North America's Morrison Formation — which dinosaur?

Found along the Andes and Pacific coasts of South America, this enormous New World vulture is one of the largest flying birds by wingspan, with males sporting a fleshy comb atop a bald red head — which species is it?
Andean condor: Species of bird. The Andean condor (Vultur gryphus) is a South American New World vulture and is the only extant member of the genus Vultur.
Also known as Umbelliferae and including carrots, celery, parsley, and dill, this plant family also contains dangerously toxic members like poison hemlock and giant hogweed — which family?
Originally conceived as the average Earth-Sun distance before its 2012 redefinition, this measure equals about 499 light-seconds and underpins the definition of the parsec — what is it called?
Astronomical unit: Mean distance between Earth and the Sun.

Baruch Goldstein: American-Israeli mass murderer (1956–1994). Goldstein was a supporter of Kach, a religious Zionist party that the United States, the European Union and other countries designate as a terrorist organization.

Having evolved independently at least 94 separate times — first in octocorals some 540 million years ago — this living glow lights up fireflies, deep-sea fish, fungi and dinoflagellates alike; what is it?
Bioluminescence: Emission of light by a living organism.

Despite lacking the tight head of typical cabbage, this leafy Chinese vegetable has a flavor often compared to spinach and water chestnuts, with a milder white bulb and stronger-tasting green leaves — what vegetable is it?
Bok choy: Subspecies of flowering plant.
With a large head, deep facial folds, and a flat face with a jutting lower jaw, this British breed's ancestors were once used for baiting cattle before the sport was banned in 1835 — which breed?
Bulldog: British breed of dog. It may also be known as the English Bulldog or British Bulldog.
First classified by Linnaeus in 1753 and indigenous to Eastern Asia, this annual flowering plant has been cultivated throughout history for fiber, oil, food, and medicine — which plant?
Cannabis sativa: Plant species. It has been cultivated throughout recorded history and used as a source of industrial fiber, seed oil, food, and medicine.

Named from a Latin word meaning 'blind,' this pouch at the start of the large intestine sits on the same side of the body as the appendix and receives chyme straight from the small intestine — which structure?
Cecum: Pouch in the large intestine. It is typically located on the right side of the body (the same side of the body as the appendix, to which it is joined).

First recorded in the 3rd-to-5th-century manuscript Sunzi Suanjing, this number-theory result lets you deduce what's left over after dividing by a product of coprime numbers, just from the leftovers after dividing by each one — which principle?
Chinese remainder theorem: About simultaneous modular congruences.
This genus of anaerobic, Gram-positive bacteria found in soil and animal intestines includes the microbes responsible for both botulism and tetanus — which genus?
Clostridium: Genus of bacteria. Species of Clostridium inhabit soils and the intestinal tracts of animals, including humans.
Named from ancient Greek for 'footless' after being mistaken for a legless swallow, this bird's closest relatives are actually hummingbirds — and it almost never touches the ground. Which bird?
Common swift: Species of bird. The resemblances between the groups are due to convergent evolution, reflecting similar contextual development.
Found in the tropics of Africa, Asia, the Americas, and Australia, this large semiaquatic reptile congregates in rivers and wetlands and is closely related to alligators and caimans — what is it?
Crocodile: Family of large reptilian carnivores.
In 1900, this mathematician presented a list of unsolved problems that shaped 20th-century mathematical research — who is he?
This linguistic term describes a combination of two vowel sounds gliding together within a single syllable, as heard five times in the phrase 'no highway cowboys' — what is it called?

Diphthong: Combination of two adjacent vowel sounds. A diphthong ( DIF-thong, DIP-), also known as a gliding vowel or a vowel glide, is a combination of two adjacent vowel sounds within the same syllable.
Named after the Greek word for 'hedgehog' because of its spiky central disk, this North American daisy relative is nicknamed the coneflower — what is it?
Echinacea: Genus of flowering plants in the daisy family.

This anaerobic parasite infects tens of millions of people worldwide, causing a gut disease whose name comes from a word meaning tissue disintegration, and kills over 55,000 people each year — what is it?
With a glossy black head and a distinctive white bill shield, this rail-family waterbird is found from Europe to Australia — which bird?
Eurasian coot: Species of bird. The Eurasian coot (Fulica atra), also known as the common coot or Australian coot, is a member of the rail and crake bird family, the Rallidae.
First synthesized by Paul Janssen in 1960 and sold under brand names like Duragesic, this synthetic opioid runs 50 to 100 times more potent than morphine — what is it?
Fentanyl: Opioid medication. Fentanyl is a highly potent synthetic opioid of the piperidine family, used primarily as pain medication.

Madagascar's largest carnivore is a slender, long-tailed mammal that climbs down trees head-first and has convergently evolved so many cat-like features it's been likened to a small cougar — yet it's no cat. What is it?
Fossa (animal): Cat-like, carnivorous mammal endemic to Madagascar.
This field studies the relationship between food and culture, encompassing everything from cooking techniques and regional cuisines to the science of good eating — what is it called?

Gastronomy: Study of the relationship between food and culture. One who is well versed in gastronomy is called a gastronome, while a gastronomist is one who unites theory and practice in the study of gastronomy.
Built from glutamate, cysteine and glycine, this tripeptide is the most abundant low-mass thiol in most cells and a key antioxidant guarding against free radicals — what is it?
Glutathione: Ubiquitous antioxidant compound in living organisms.

Native to Africa and among the oldest of the chicken-like Galliformes birds, one domesticated species of this family wears a distinctive helmet-shaped casque and has been introduced worldwide — what are they?
Guinea fowl: Family of birds. Guinea fowl or guineafowl are birds of the family Numididae in the order Galliformes.
This localized pooling of blood outside the vessels — often triggered by injury, surgery, or blood-thinning medication — starts out liquid before clotting solid within the tissue. What is it called?
Hematoma: Localized bleeding outside of blood vessels. An ecchymosis is a hematoma of the skin larger than 10 mm.
Ashy-grey with a black head, throat and wings, this corvid was split into its own species in 2002 only to be folded back into its all-black relative by a 2025 reclassification — name the bird?
Hooded crow: Species of bird. The hooded crow (Corvus corone cornix), also colloquially called just hoodie, is a Eurasian bird subspecies of the carrion crow (Corvus corone) in the genus Corvus.

Defined as a blood sodium level below 135 millimoles per liter, this condition can arise from drinking excessive water — or even too much beer — and in severe cases causes seizures or coma — what is it?
Hyponatremia: Low sodium concentration in the blood.

Also known by names meaning 'water spinach' and 'kangkung,' this semi-aquatic tropical vegetable was likely first domesticated in Southeast Asia and thrives with barely any care near waterways — which plant is it?
Ipomoea aquatica: Species of plant. Ipomoea aquatica, commonly known as water spinach or kangkung, is a semi-aquatic, tropical plant grown as a vegetable for its tender shoots.
Serving as special adviser to the UN Secretary-General from 2002 to 2018, which Columbia University economist co-founded a nonprofit dedicated to ending extreme poverty?
Developed by a South Korean aerospace firm with Lockheed Martin and first flown in 2002, this supersonic jet trainer became the country's first indigenous supersonic aircraft — which aircraft family?
KAI T-50 Golden Eagle: Family of South Korean jet aircraft. It is South Korea's first indigenous supersonic aircraft and one of the world's few supersonic trainers.

Until a 2020 taxonomic overhaul split many of its 261 species into 25 new genera, this rod-shaped, gram-positive bacterial genus formed a major part of the human gut and vaginal microbiota — what genus?
Lactobacillus: Genus of bacteria. Lactobacillus forms biofilms in the vaginal and gut microbiota, allowing them to persist in harsh environmental conditions and maintain ample populations.
This Chinese herbalist, martial artist, and tactical advisor died in 1933 having allegedly been born in 1677 — a longevity claim gerontologists dismiss as myth. Who was he?
Li Ching-Yuen: Chinese herbalist (died 1933). Li's year of birth was alleged to be 1677, though his true age has never been determined.
This Berkeley professor gave us "fuzzy" everything — fuzzy sets, fuzzy logic, fuzzy control — proposing a whole branch of mathematics for reasoning with imprecision. Who was he?
Defined by milk-producing glands, hair or fur, a broad neocortex, and three tiny middle-ear bones, this animal class split from reptile-and-bird ancestors over 300 million years ago — what is it?
Mammal: Class of animals with milk-producing glands.

Marked by small white Koplik spots inside the mouth and a red rash that starts on the face before spreading, this highly contagious, vaccine-preventable disease can bring fevers over 40°C — which disease?
This development economist shared the 2019 Nobel with Esther Duflo and Abhijit Banerjee for an experimental approach to fighting global poverty — who is he?
Michael Kremer: American economist and Nobel laureate (born 1964)
Originally a dry-season staple for ǃKung hunter-gatherers, this tropical vine in the Cucurbitaceae family produces an intensely bitter edible fruit widely used across Asian cuisine — what is it?
Momordica charantia: Species of plant in the gourd family.
Found in cardiac and skeletal muscle and distantly related to hemoglobin, high levels of this oxygen-storing protein let diving whales and seals hold their breath longer — which protein?
Also known as black cumin or kalonji, this flowering plant native to the Levant and Iran is used across the world as a culinary spice — which species is it?
Nigella sativa: Species of flowering plant in the buttercup family.
Native to the Democratic Republic of the Congo, this striped mammal looks like a zebra crossbred with a giraffe but is actually the giraffe's closest living relative — which animal?
Okapi: Species of mammal. Although the okapi has striped markings reminiscent of zebras, it is most closely related to the giraffe.
A reactive nonmetal of the chalcogen group, it's the most abundant element in Earth's crust — locked into water, silicates, and rust — and the third-most abundant in the universe. What is it?
Oxygen: Chemical element with atomic number 8 (O)
Carl Linnaeus named this crop 'hypogaea' — Greek for 'under the earth' — because, unlike most legumes, it ripens its pods below ground. What is it?
Peanut: Legume cultivated as a grain and oil crop.
Its name combines the Greek words for 'love' and 'tree,' and with over 600 accepted species it's the second-largest genus in the arum family after Anthurium — which popular houseplant genus?
Known informally for resembling a certain dairy product due to its shape, this popular edible fungus grows wild across temperate and subtropical forests worldwide — what is its scientific name?
First prescribed in 1934, this steroid sex hormone plays a key role in the menstrual cycle, pregnancy, and embryonic development — what is it?
Progesterone: Sex hormone. Progesterone (P4) is an endogenous steroid and progestogen sex hormone involved in the menstrual cycle, pregnancy, and embryogenesis of humans and other species.
This is the name for three positive whole numbers a, b, and c satisfying a² + b² = c², like the classic set (3, 4, 5) — what is it called?
Pythagorean triple: Integer side lengths of a right triangle.
Spanning turtles, crocodilians, the lizards-and-snakes of Squamata, and the lone tuatara, which group of ectothermic, amniotic animals does herpetology study?
Reptile: Class of animals. The study of the traditional reptile orders, customarily in combination with the study of modern amphibians, is called herpetology.
With over three hundred species and tens of thousands of cultivars, this thorny, often-fragrant flowering shrub blooms in shades from white to pink, red, orange, and yellow — which plant?

First used in English in the early 15th century and possibly named after a Mediterranean island, this term covers small oily forage fish under 15 centimeters, with larger ones called pilchards — what's the fish?
Sardine: Common name for various small, oily forage fish.
A slender African cat with a tiny head and enormous ears, this golden, black-spotted hunter is the sole member of its genus and stands tall on remarkably long legs — which wild cat is it?
